fields.description: One digest per room, and the docname IS the room - so 'two workers generated a digest for the same room at once' is a failed insert rather than two summaries that disagree. There is no second uniqueness rule to keep in sync.
fields.label: Room

fields.description: Monotonic, bumped on every republish. It is embedded in every cache key derived from this digest, which is what makes an invalidation actually invalidate: without it, a re-generated summary keeps the key of the one it replaced and the old text is served until the TTL happens to roll.
fields.label: Digest Version

fields.description: How many times this digest has been rolled forward incrementally. At the configured ceiling the next pass is a FULL rebuild from source messages regardless of staleness, because a summary of a summary of a summary drifts from the transcript in ways nothing measures.
fields.label: Generation Count

fields.description: Set by the staleness seam when an edit or a delete lands inside the covered span. RETRIEVAL SKIPS A STALE DIGEST OUTRIGHT rather than serving it with a caveat, and the rebuild is a full regeneration from source, never an incremental append: a rolling summary can add information but it cannot unsay it. This is the mechanism that stops a deleted sentence surviving in a model's context window after the person who wrote it deleted it.
fields.label: Is Stale

fields.description: First value of the three-value watermark: the highest seq covered. Necessary and NOT sufficient on its own - an edit and a delete both leave seq untouched, so a digest keyed on seq alone is unchanged by a delete, its cache key is unchanged, and the summary containing the deleted message is served again.
fields.label: Watermark Seq

fields.description: Second value: how many messages the summary was built from. This is the one that catches a HARD delete, which moves neither seq nor modified.
fields.label: Watermark Count

fields.description: Third value: max(modified) across the covered messages, which is what catches an EDIT. Compared using frappe.utils.now_datetime() on both sides or converted explicitly, never against SQL NOW(): the production database runs UTC while Frappe writes creation/modified in site-local time, so a naive TIMESTAMPDIFF reports a row written one minute ago as six hours old and every freshness predicate built on it is wrong in the same direction.
fields.label: Watermark Modified

fields.description: The seq span this summary describes, inclusive. An edit or delete whose message falls inside [covered_from, covered_to] is what sets is_stale - which is why the span is stored rather than inferred from the watermark.
fields.label: Covered From

fields.description: Wall-clock bounds of the covered span. A span older than the configured age forces a full rebuild even when nothing is stale, because a rolling summary of a year of conversation is a summary of nothing in particular.
fields.label: Covered From At

fields.description: The rendered summary, a few hundred tokens. It is DERIVED from employee-private conversation and is therefore exactly as sensitive as the conversation - more so in one respect, because a summary crosses time and topic boundaries that a single message does not. Zero DocPerm, same as Chat Message.
fields.label: Summary Text

fields.description: When this digest was last produced. The health check alerts when the newest generated_at across all digests is older than the configured window - the failure being watched for is not an error, it is silence.
fields.label: Generated At

fields.description: Consecutive rebuild failures. The poison-pill guard: at the configured ceiling the room stops being scheduled for rebuild and an alert is raised, because a digest that fails every five minutes forever is a job that fills the Error Log until nobody reads it.
fields.label: Rebuild Failures

fields.description: Set when rebuild_failures hits the ceiling. The digest stays stale, stays unserved, and stops being retried until a human clears this. Deliberately a separate flag from is_stale: 'nobody has rebuilt this yet' and 'this cannot be rebuilt' need different answers from an operator.
fields.label: Poisoned

fields.description: The last failure, scrubbed. Never a message body.
fields.label: Last Error
